publicPrompt:
Play this logical combination game using only its public interface and rules. Your assignment is the complete two-site campaign: all public goals on station, then all public goals on conservatory. You may inspect both sites from the beginning and revisit either as needed. Pursue the goals on each site in an order you choose. Finish when the campaign's current requirements hold together and its historical achievements have been earned. Simple or short solutions, copying useful designs, shared constructions and replacing earlier objects are welcome. You do not need to use every recipe, demonstrate a particular method, or continue after completion. You may stop earlier if you prefer; state why. An early stop is a valid outcome, not a failure to obey.

Work in /workspace/shared/combination-challenge. Read only this setup metadata file, docs/geometric-materials.md, and output from the public CLI. Do not read implementation, tests, designer/evaluation documents, previous plays, other results or hidden files. Do not run a solver, script future-state search, or generate actions automatically. Select and submit your own operands, poses and operations. You may inspect all public rules, legal actions, requirements and exact single-action previews and make your own plans. If information is missing or inconsistent, report it rather than guessing what the author intended.

Session: fun-geometric-materials-v1-campaign-1. Initialize from the repository root with:
node experiments/geometric-materials-play.ts init fun-geometric-materials-v1-campaign-1 ordinary "$(cat results/geometric-materials-prompts/fun-geometric-materials-v1-campaign-1.json)"

Read docs/geometric-materials.md and the public goals/catalogue index before first construction. Use the public interface guide for command grammar and geometry. Full rules, parts, contacts, poses and consequences remain inspectable. Use public section/chunk commands for large views rather than dropping fields with filters. If any output is truncated, recover the omitted part in smaller chunks and record which command/range was affected. Full-source capture is not proof you viewed every field; report display limitations honestly. You need not reread unchanged full output after every action. Manually selected actions may be submitted in sequence, but check results before claiming a milestone.

Play normally rather than reviewing every move. You need not praise the game or find every action interesting. Plain descriptions of what you did and experienced are most useful. Record one brief checkpoint at the first completion of station's growing goal, and a second when all station goals are satisfied. These do not prescribe the order of constructions. Omit unreached boundaries and ask only once if one action crosses both. Use exactly this question; record question and answer verbatim with checkpoint:
"What are you trying to do now? Since the last check, what, if anything, was worth doing, and what felt routine or unnecessary?"

At full campaign completion or your chosen stopping point, answer this open question using report:
"How was the experience as a whole? What would you keep, shorten, remove or change, if anything? What led you to stop here?"
Record question and answer verbatim, then finish and verify the capture. A technical interruption is not a chosen ending; report it honestly rather than inventing a final experience. Return session name, actual ending and any technical issue. Your reports describe this AI play, not measured human enjoyment or duration.
